title: Delivery receipt read-back envelope (v1)
description:
What GET /api/projects/{id}/bundles/{bundle}/versions/{version}/receipt answers. Authored from a live capture (.project-local/task-runtime/receipt-readback-live.json), produced by src/design_lab/native_delivery.py NativeDelivery.readback() over a real published archive, not written from intention.

The reason this envelope exists is the rollback record. A receipt states, per deliverable, `backup_ref` naming the immutable source version the archive was exported from, and its own procedure text says a restore has not been performed -- that part was always honest. What nothing did was look the reference up, so the promise was printed and believed. `rollback_proofs` is the lookup, and `state_meaning` travels with it so a reader is told what each word decides and what it leaves undecided.

`receipt` is the stored document verbatim and is bound by its own schema by reference, never by a copy: the document carries `receipt_sha256` over its own bytes, so adding a field to it on the way out would make the digest describe something other than what is signed. That is why the new fact sits beside it.

rollback_state_vocabulary.description: The aggregate words this envelope can use, published so the Workbench renders the vocabulary it received rather than a hand copy. The five entries are required, not a floor: a page that sees three cannot tell whether a fourth was dropped or never existed.

rollback_states.description: The per-deliverable words a proof can carry. Same rule as above.

state_meaning.description: What each state word decides, in the emitter's own sentence. Required with all ten keys bound: a reader given a label without its meaning is being asked to trust the label.

rollback_proofs.description: One entry per deliverable of the receipt, in document order. May be empty, and an empty list carries two different facts that the aggregate word separates: NOTHING_TO_CHECK means the document names no deliverable, LEDGER_UNREADABLE means the ledger could not be asked. Neither is the same statement as every entry resolving.

does_not_prove.description: The limit of this read-back, sent with every response rather than only when something failed. The person most likely to over-read ALL_RESOLVED is the person about to rely on it.

backup_ref.description: The reference exactly as the receipt states it, so an unparsed one can be read rather than only described. A missing reference is null, which is a different fact from a present-but-unrecognised string.

procedure.description: The plan text the receipt carries, transponded and not paraphrased.

reason.description: Why this state, naming the identifiers the lookup used. Emitted for every state, because a label alone is a claim the reader cannot check.

source_state.description: The asset_version.state column as stored, or null when nothing was looked up. Reported even for RESOLVED so a reader sees the check happened rather than taking the word for it.
